version.changelog: fix(v1.6.0): watchdog 12-day silent failure due to path encoding bug

llm.summary: The main UI patch is locally scoped and mostly disclosed, but the package also includes an optional Windows scheduled-task watchdog that the main skill says is not part of the artifact.

dimensions.detail: The injected browser script uses a MutationObserver, a 1-second self-heal heartbeat, localStorage/sessionStorage, and a same-origin fetch('./') every 5 minutes that may reload the tab after updates. These behaviors are disclosed and purpose-related, but they go beyond a passive UI tweak.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The installer uses PowerShell with ExecutionPolicy Bypass, auto-detects the OpenClaw Control UI directory, backs up index.html, injects or replaces one script tag, copies a versioned JS asset, and removes only matching older pcl-model-picker.v*.js files. This is side-effecting but scoped and reversible.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The main SKILL.md discloses the local patch and same-origin update polling, but it also says the watchdog is not part of the ClawHub artifact while artifact/platform/pcl-watchdog.ps1 is actually included. The trigger language is also broad for a skill that can modify an installed application.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The core patch persists until uninstall or OpenClaw upgrade by modifying the installed UI. More importantly, the included optional watchdog can register a recurring Windows scheduled task that runs hidden PowerShell to repair the patch, while the main skill text under-discloses its presence in this artifact.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core behavior matches the stated purpose: it patches OpenClaw Control UI index.html, adds a model-picker browser script, hides the account row in that picker, and provides uninstall instructions. No external telemetry or credential handling was found in the inspected core path.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to let the skill modify your local OpenClaw Control UI files. Treat the platform watchdog separately: do not run its -Install mode unless you explicitly want a recurring hidden Windows scheduled task that repairs the patch after upgrades. Use the documented -Remove command for the core patch and the watchdog -Uninstall command if you register it.
llm.findings:
[RA1] expected: The self-update references describe the installed UI enhancement checking for a newer same-origin app shell and reloading, plus an optional repair watchdog; this is not evidence of the skill modifying its own SKILL.md or agent instructions.
[TM1] expected: The schtasks delete command is limited to removing the named watchdog scheduled task during uninstall, not arbitrary task deletion.
[LP1] expected: The browser-side network use is a same-origin fetch('./') for update detection and is disclosed in the current SKILL.md; no external network endpoint or telemetry was found.
[P2] expected: The flagged content is a BOM, comments, and an HTML marker used by the patch script; I did not find hidden agent directives or prompt-injection instructions in those snippets.
[AE4] expected: The mixed-script content is consistent with multilingual documentation and Chinese comments; it was not evidence of obfuscation or secret handling.
[SDI-1] expected: The self-update watchdog is real: it polls same-origin HTML and can reload the page. It is disclosed and scoped, but users should know it adds autonomous browser behavior.
[SQP-2] expected: The silent same-origin polling and reload behavior exists and is purpose-related, but it can affect active sessions; the script tries to delay reload while typing.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The activation language could cause a side-effecting install or repair workflow from a broad model-picker complaint unless the agent obtains clear user intent first.
[SQP-3] expected: The language and translation findings are not material security concerns for this artifact review.
[SDI-2] expected: The exported window diagnostic helpers are disclosed in the verification instructions and expose local UI diagnostic state rather than credentials.
